answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused to reopen pricing and an 18% cost cut is mandated—renegotiation is blocked. Renewing at current terms will miss the cost target. Deferring sacrifices control and leaves us exposed at month-to-month rates. Adding a second source buys time but doesn't solve the immediate 18% gap. Switching to the low-cost vendor (memory_c2) delivered sharp unit cost reduction and quick onboarding before; memory_c6 shows that multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing. At 94% line utilization, switching carries real delivery risk, but the financial mandate and incumbent's refusal to negotiate force a choice between cost target and incumbent stability. Verifying memory_c2 (prior low-cost switch success) and memory_c6 (volume pricing leverage) will confirm whether a switch can be executed within 14 days and whether a short-term commitment can meet the 18% target while preserving some upside optionality. Standard_experiment scale limits exposure to 1–2 SKUs or a defined trial period before full transition, reducing line risk while testing the low-cost vendor's performance at current volumes.
